highlights.text: Taichi: "D-dummy, my heart of hearts is crying, baka! Wailing, baka! This is the utsuge route!"

adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "None of that I can seee～."
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, role reversal, or independently actionable English defect.

adjudicated.jp: 「男同士でジメジメしたって寒いだけだ、そーいうイベントは貴様のねーちゃんと起こすわい」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "But it's corny to get all tearful with males! Go trigger that event with your nee-chan, you bastard!"
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator says he will trigger that sentimental event with Tomoki's sister instead. 'Go trigger that event' orders Tomoki to do it, reversing the agent; 'nee-chan' is also left untranslated.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I'll save that kind of event for your sister.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "But it's corny to get all tearful with males! Go trigger that event with your nee-chan, you bastard!"

adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "Nastyyy!"
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, role reversal, or independently actionable English defect.

adjudicated.jp: 「さあ、そうと決まったらとっとと働け！　放送予定日は明日じゃい」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Well, if that's your decision then get to work you whelp! Broadcast's scheduled for tomorrow ya know."
adjudicated.assessment: そうと決まったら means 'now that that's settled.' 'If that's your decision' assigns the decision specifically to Tomoki, and 'you whelp' adds an insult absent from the source.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Now that that's settled, get to work! The broadcast is tomorrow.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Well, if that's your decision then get to work you whelp! Broadcast's scheduled for tomorrow ya know."

adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "Yeah, yeah."
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, role reversal, or independently actionable English defect.

adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, role reversal, or independently actionable English defect.

adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "...Taichi?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, role reversal, or independently actionable English defect.

adjudicated.jp: 校舎に戻る足を止め、友貴。
adjudicated.en: A leg inside the school building, Tomoki stops.
adjudicated.assessment: The source says Tomoki stops on his way back into the school building. 'A leg inside the school building, Tomoki stops' turns the route into a body part and is not grammatical English.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'On his way back into the school building, Tomoki stops.'

highlights.text: A leg inside the school building, Tomoki stops.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Hm?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, role reversal, or independently actionable English defect.

adjudicated.jp: 「……てっきり姉貴と仲直りしろとか言うのかなって思ってた、姉貴を手伝えよ弟だろって」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "...I thought you would tell me to put things right with Aneki, for sure, that a younger brother should help his Aneki."
adjudicated.assessment: 姉貴 is left untranslated twice as 'Aneki,' and the reported expectations are assembled as a run-on rather than two parallel things Taichi might say.
adjudicated.remedy: Use '...I was sure you'd tell me to make up with my sister, or say that as her brother I ought to help her.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "...I thought you would tell me to put things right with Aneki, for sure, that a younger brother should help his Aneki."

adjudicated.jp: 「いや、姉弟喧嘩なんてごくまっとうな人生じゃん。止めんよ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Naaah, sibling quarreling's a very respectable way of life it is. Don'tcha stop."
adjudicated.assessment: 止めんよ means the speaker will not interfere with or stop the siblings' quarrel. 'Don'tcha stop' changes the first-person decision into an imperative telling Tomoki to continue.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'No. A sibling quarrel is a perfectly normal part of life. I won't interfere.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Naaah, sibling quarreling's a very respectable way of life it is. Don'tcha stop."

adjudicated.jp: 「要するに俺様を手伝えということだ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Basically this is about you helping the greatness that is I."
adjudicated.assessment: 'The greatness that is I' uses the wrong pronoun case and awkwardly expands 俺様.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'In short, you're here to help the great me.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Basically this is about you helping the greatness that is I."

adjudicated.en: Puff that chest with pride!
adjudicated.assessment: 胸を張る is the narrator's present action of throwing out his chest. 'Puff that chest with pride!' changes it into an imperative addressed to someone else.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I puff out my chest.'

highlights.text: Puff that chest with pride!

adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "...what're you a VIP."
adjudicated.assessment: おまえ大物 is an impressed or incredulous judgment that the addressee is really something. 'What're you a VIP' is not grammatical and treats 大物 as a literal status question.
adjudicated.remedy: Use '...You really are something.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "...what're you a VIP."

adjudicated.jp: 「適応係数８０オーバーのオーバーロードですから」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "After all, I am the Overlord of all those of Conformity Coefficient 80 and Over."
adjudicated.assessment: The source says the speaker is an Overlord with an adaptation coefficient above eighty. The English makes him ruler 'of all those' above eighty, adding a hierarchy and other people.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I'm an Overlord with an adaptation coefficient over eighty.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "After all, I am the Overlord of all those of Conformity Coefficient 80 and Over."

adjudicated.jp: 「……そのオーバーロードとも、これからも普通に友達してやるよ」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "...and I will still be this Overlord's normal friend from now on."
adjudicated.assessment: The source promises to keep treating even this self-styled Overlord as an ordinary friend. 'This Overlord's normal friend' turns 'ordinary' into a property of the friend and muddles the continuing relationship.
adjudicated.remedy: Use '...Even with an Overlord like that, I'll go on being your friend like normal.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "...and I will still be this Overlord's normal friend from now on."

adjudicated.jp: 「そういうの、嫌いじゃないから」
adjudicated.en: Tomoki: "Because... I don't hate that of you."
adjudicated.assessment: そういうの refers to that kind of behavior or attitude. 'That of you' is ungrammatical and changes the demonstrative into a property possessed by the addressee.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I don't dislike that kind of thing.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Because... I don't hate that of you."

adjudicated.jp: さっと校舎内に消えた。逃げるように。
adjudicated.en: He quickly vanishes inside the school building. As if running away.
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, role reversal, or independently actionable English defect.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "'Iiii don't haaate that of youuu'... pffft!"
adjudicated.assessment: The line mockingly repeats the immediately preceding sentiment. 'That of you' remains ungrammatical even inside the imitation and obscures the exact callback.
adjudicated.remedy: Mock the established English line while preserving its wording, for example 'I don't disliiike that kind of thiiing...'

highlights.text: Taichi: "'Iiii don't haaate that of youuu'... pffft!"

adjudicated.jp: そう言った友貴は、一瞬で人類の限界まで赤面しきっていた。
adjudicated.en: After Tomoki had said that, his face had instantly reddened up to the physical blushing limits of mankind.
adjudicated.assessment: 'Reddened up to the physical blushing limits of mankind' is an over-literal and syntactically congested rendering of the hyperbole that he blushed to the human limit.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Tomoki had instantly turned as red as humanly possible.'

highlights.text: After Tomoki had said that, his face had instantly reddened up to the physical blushing limits of mankind.

adjudicated.jp: 「照れるくらいなら言うんじゃねーっての。まったく」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "If it makes you embarrassed then don'tcha say it! Seriously."
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, role reversal, or independently actionable English defect.

adjudicated.en: I look up at the antenna.
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, role reversal, or independently actionable English defect.

adjudicated.jp: 「でも、これでちっとは進捗すんな」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "But with this, we're a little on the way aren't we."
adjudicated.assessment: ちっとは進捗する says this will produce at least a little progress. 'We're a little on the way' is not idiomatic English and turns the progress into physical position.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Still, this should move things along a little.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "But with this, we're a little on the way aren't we."

adjudicated.en: Fun pretend-a-club-activities.
adjudicated.assessment: 部活ごっこ is playing or pretending at club activities. 'Pretend-a-club-activities' is not a coherent English compound.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Our fun little game of pretending to be a club.'

highlights.text: Fun pretend-a-club-activities.

adjudicated.jp: 大切な思い出となりえる。
adjudicated.en: They may become precious memories.
adjudicated.assessment: The singular activity just named could become a precious memory. 'They may become' supplies a plural subject with no stable antecedent.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'It could become a precious memory.'

highlights.text: They may become precious memories.

adjudicated.en: Forever.
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, role reversal, or independently actionable English defect.

adjudicated.jp: ありがとうと、思うため。
adjudicated.en: For the sake of thinking... thank you.
adjudicated.assessment: The source expresses the purpose of someday being able to think or say 'thank you.' 'For the sake of thinking... thank you' does not form a grammatical English relation between purpose and quoted thought.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'So that I can think: thank you.'

highlights.text: For the sake of thinking... thank you.

adjudicated.jp: 俺は戦っているんだと思う。
adjudicated.en: I will be fighting.
comments: Assuming this is an older revision for hopefully obvious reasons. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 俺は戦っているんだと思う is a present reflective claim: 'I think this is what I'm fighting for.' The English changes it to future tense and omits the governing 'I think.'
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I think that is what I am fighting for.'

highlights.text: I will be fighting.
